ukmt-sk-2019-01.title: Pair the factors
ukmt-sk-2019-01.body:
The factor pairs are $1\cdot144$, $2\cdot72$, $3\cdot48$, $4\cdot36$, $6\cdot24$, $8\cdot18$, $9\cdot16$, and $12$ on its own. The sum is $145+74+51+40+30+26+25+12=403$.

**Answer: 403**

ukmt-sk-2019-01.title: Use the formula
ukmt-sk-2019-01.body:
$144=2^4\cdot3^2$, so the sum of the factors is $(1+2+4+8+16)(1+3+9)=31\cdot13=403$.

**Answer: 403**

ukmt-sk-2019-03.title: Four right triangles
ukmt-sk-2019-03.body:
Let the diagonals meet at $M$ and split into lengths $a,c$ (total $14$) and $b,d$ (total $30$). The quadrilateral is made of four right triangles with areas $\frac12ab,\frac12bc,\frac12cd,\frac12da$, whose sum is $\frac12(a+c)(b+d)=\frac12\cdot14\cdot30=210$.

**Answer: 210**

ukmt-sk-2019-04.title: Sum the terms
ukmt-sk-2019-04.body:
There are $21$ terms, with sum $21n+(1+2+\dots+20)=21n+210$. Then $21n+210>2019$ gives $21n>1809$, i.e. $n>86.14\ldots$, so the smallest integer is $87$.

**Answer: 87**

ukmt-sk-2019-05.title: Angles around a vertex
ukmt-sk-2019-05.body:
Each interior angle of a regular pentagon is $108^\circ$. At a vertex of the inner polygon, two pentagons and the polygon meet, so its interior angle is $360^\circ-2\cdot108^\circ=144^\circ$, an exterior angle of $36^\circ$, hence $\frac{360}{36}=10$ sides. Each side equals a pentagon side, $\frac{65}5=13$. So $P=10\cdot13=130$.

**Answer: 130**

ukmt-sk-2019-06.title: Difference of squares
ukmt-sk-2019-06.body:
$2019=(a-b)(a+b)=3\cdot673$ with $673$ prime, so the factor pairs are $(1,2019)$ and $(3,673)$. They give $(a,b)=(1010,1009)$ and $(338,335)$. Since $a<1000$, $a=338$.

**Answer: 338**

ukmt-sk-2019-07.title: Two conditions
ukmt-sk-2019-07.body:
$3n+1$ has three digits when $100\le3n+1\le999$, i.e. $33\le n\le332$. $\frac{n+1}3$ is a three-digit integer when $3\mid n+1$ and $300\le n+1\le2997$, so $n\ge299$. Combining: $299\le n\le332$ with $n+1$ divisible by $3$, i.e. $n+1\in\{300,303,\dots,333\}$: that is $12$ values.

**Answer: 12**

ukmt-sk-2019-08.title: Work backwards
ukmt-sk-2019-08.body:
$J(t)=0$ only for $t=0$ and $t=-4$. So $J(J(x))=0$ requires $J(x)\in\{0,-4\}$: $J(x)=0$ gives $x\in\{0,-4\}$ and $J(x)=-4$ gives $x=-8$ (only the branch $4+x$ reaches $-4$; the other branches give values $\ge0$). Then $J(J(J(x)))=0$ requires $J(J(x))\in\{0,-4\}$, i.e. $J(x)\in\{0,-4\}$ or $J(x)=-8$; the last has the single solution $x=-12$. The solutions are $x=0,-4,-8,-12$: $4$ in all.

**Answer: 4**

ukmt-sk-2019-09.title: Find a representation of 100
ukmt-sk-2019-09.body:
The smallest three-digit number is $100$, so it is enough to show that $100$ can be written in this form: with $a=2$, $b=6$ we get $2^6+6^2=64+36=100$.

**Answer: 100**

ukmt-sk-2019-10.title: Difference of squares
ukmt-sk-2019-10.body:
The first two factors multiply to $\sqrt{169-(28+\sqrt{281})}=\sqrt{141-\sqrt{281}}$. Then $\sqrt{141-\sqrt{281}}\sqrt{141+\sqrt{281}}=\sqrt{141^2-281}=\sqrt{19881-281}=\sqrt{19600}=140$.

**Answer: 140**

ukmt-sk-2019-14.title: Count exponents
ukmt-sk-2019-14.body:
$N^5=p^5q^5r^5$. Each factor is $p^aq^br^c$ with $0\le a,b,c\le5$: $6\cdot6\cdot6=216$ factors.

**Answer: 216**

ukmt-sk-2019-15.title: Count each line twice
ukmt-sk-2019-15.body:
Each of the $10$ lines is counted twice in the announced totals (once by each end). So the paint needed is $\frac12(17+43+56+66+76)=\frac{258}2=129$.

**Answer: 129**

ukmt-sk-2019-16.title: Subtract the equations
ukmt-sk-2019-16.body:
Subtracting gives $x+y=28$. Substituting $y=28-x$ into $xy-x=180$: $x(27-x)=180$, so $x^2-27x+180=0$ and $x=12$ or $15$. The solutions are $(15,13)$ and $(12,16)$. The required value is $15+130+12+160=317$.

**Answer: 317**

ukmt-sk-2019-17.title: Extend $BA$
ukmt-sk-2019-17.body:
Extend $BA$ beyond $A$ to $N$ with $CN\parallel MA$. Since $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$, $A$ is the midpoint of $BN$, so $AN=AB=123$. Also $CN\perp AB$ (as $MA\perp AB$), and $\angle CAN=180^\circ-120^\circ=60^\circ$. In right triangle $ANC$: $\cos60^\circ=\frac{AN}{AC}$, so $AC=\frac{123}{1/2}=246$.

**Answer: 246**

ukmt-sk-2019-17.title: Coordinates
ukmt-sk-2019-17.body:
Put $A=(0,0)$, $B=(-123,0)$, $M=(0,m)$. Then $C=2M-B=(123,2m)$. $\angle BAC=120^\circ$ gives $\cos120^\circ=\frac{\vec{AB}\cdot\vec{AC}}{AB\cdot AC}=\frac{-123^2}{123\,AC}$, so $-\frac12=-\frac{123}{AC}$ and $AC=246$.

**Answer: 246**

ukmt-sk-2019-18.title: Check two-digit and three-digit numbers
ukmt-sk-2019-18.body:
For a two-digit $N=10a+b$ to be chunky we need $a\mid N$, hence $a\mid b$, and $b\mid N$, hence $b\mid10a$. Going through the tens digit: $a=1$: $15$ (and $11,12$, which are below $13$); $a=2$: $22,24$ ($26$ and $28$ fail); $a=3$: $33,36$ ($39$ fails); $a=4$: $44,48$; $a=5,6,7,8,9$: only $55,66,77,88,99$. That is $12$ two-digit chunky numbers in range.

Among $100,\dots,112$, those from $100$ to $110$ contain a zero, and $111$ and $112$ are chunky. Total $12+2=14$.

**Answer: 14**

ukmt-sk-2019-19.title: Coordinates
ukmt-sk-2019-19.body:
Let $B=(0,0)$, $A=(0,105)$, $C=(105,0)$, $D=(105,105)$ (a square with $BD$ along $y=x$). $M=(52.5,0)$ and $N=(26.25,0)$. Line $AM$: $y=105-2x$ meets $y=x$ at $x=35$: $P=(35,35)$. Line $AN$: $y=105-4x$ meets $y=x$ at $x=21$: $Q=(21,21)$. Area of $APQ$ with $A=(0,105)$: $\frac12\,|PQ|\cdot\text{dist}(A,BD)=\frac12\cdot14\sqrt2\cdot\frac{105}{\sqrt2}=735$.

**Answer: 735**

ukmt-sk-2019-20.title: Deduce the digits
ukmt-sk-2019-20.body:
$1001=7\cdot11\cdot13$, so 1 across is $77$ or $91$ (the composite two-digit factors). 1 down starts with that digit and lies between two primes: starting with $7$, $72$ works ($71$ and $73$ are prime); no number starting with $9$ works. So 1 across is $77$ and 1 down is $72$; 3 across therefore starts with $2$.

For $pq^3$ and $p^3q$ to both be two-digit numbers, $\{p,q\}=\{2,3\}$, giving $2\cdot27=54$ and $3\cdot8=24$. 4 down starts with the last digit of 3 across. If 4 down were $24$, then 3 across would be $2\,?\,2$, a palindrome, which is not allowed. So 4 down is $54$ and 5 across is $24$; 3 across ends in $5$.

2 down starts with $7$ (the second digit of 1 across), ends with $2$ (the first digit of 5 across) and is a multiple of $9$: $702$ or $792$. All digits are non-zero, so it is $792$. The middle digit of 3 across is the middle digit of 2 down, $9$. So 3 across is $295$.

**Answer: 295**
